title: Construction of the kernel-normalized determinant isomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $a:P\to Q$ a morphism of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], both zero outside degrees $-1,0$, whose terms are direct summands of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Suppose $a^{-1},a^0$ are surjective and the induced maps on $H^{-1}$ and $H^0$ are isomorphisms. Put $N^i=\ker a^i$, with the restricted differential $d_N$. Then each sequence $0\to N^i\to P^i\to Q^i\to0$ splits, $N^i$ is finite projective, and $d_N:N^{-1}\to N^0$ is an isomorphism. For a finite projective module $V$, let $\det_R(V)$ be its determinant line, locally its top exterior power, with kernel-first exact-sequence maps $\gamma^i:\det_R(N^i)\otimes_R\det_R(Q^i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\det_R(P^i)$ as in [lem-trf-projective-determinant-exact-sequence]. For any such two-term complex $E$ put $D(E)=\det_R(E^0)\otimes_R\det_R(E^{-1})^\vee$, where $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$. Let $\Gamma_a:D(Q)\otimes_R D(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(P)$ be obtained by tensoring $\gamma^0$ with the inverse dual of $\gamma^{-1}$ and reordering factors by ordinary tensor symmetry. The element $\delta_N\in D(N)$ corresponding to $\det(d_N)$ under $D(N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(\det_R(N^{-1}),\det_R(N^0))$ generates this invertible module. Consequently $x\mapsto\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)$ is an isomorphism $D(Q)\to D(P)$ and has a unique inverse $T_a:D(P)\to D(Q)$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), construction preceding Tag 0FJJ, together with Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses).

proof.text: Projective lifting applied to $1_{Q^i}$ along the surjection $a^i$ gives a section $s_i:Q^i\to P^i$. The mutually inverse maps $N^i\oplus Q^i\to P^i$, $(n,q)\mapsto n+s_iq$, and $p\mapsto(p-s_ia^ip,a^ip)$ split the exact sequence. Thus $N^i$ is a direct summand of $P^i$, hence of a finite free module: compose its inclusion and projection with a finite-free splitting of $P^i$. The composite projection after inclusion is the identity.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), the kernel term exact sequences; explicit projective lifting expansion.

proof.text: The chain-map equation $a^0d_P=d_Qa^{-1}$ restricts $d_P$ to $d_N:N^{-1}\to N^0$. If $n\in N^{-1}$ and $d_Nn=0$, then $n$ lies in $H^{-1}(P)=\ker d_P$. Its image in $H^{-1}(Q)$ is zero, so injectivity of $H^{-1}(a)$ gives $n=0$. There are no incoming boundaries in degree $-1$. Thus $d_N$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), acyclicity of the kernel, injectivity in the two-term case.

proof.text: For $n\in N^0$, its class in $H^0(P)=P^0/d_PP^{-1}$ maps to zero. Injectivity of $H^0(a)$ gives $p\in P^{-1}$ with $d_Pp=n$. Then $a^{-1}p$ is a cycle of $Q$. Surjectivity of $H^{-1}(a)$ gives a cycle $z\in P^{-1}$ with $a^{-1}z=a^{-1}p$; equality is of actual cycles because there are no degree-$-1$ boundaries. Hence $p-z\in N^{-1}$ and $d_N(p-z)=n$. This proves surjectivity. The inverse of the bijective linear map $d_N$ is linear by uniqueness of preimages, so $d_N$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), acyclicity of the kernel, surjectivity in the two-term case.

proof.text: Apply the kernel-first determinant exact-sequence theorem to the two split exact sequences. Its hypotheses hold by step 1 and the finite projectivity of the given terms. It supplies exactly $\gamma^i:\det_R(N^i)\otimes\det_R(Q^i)\cong\det_R(P^i)$ and says that all these determinant modules are finite projective and locally free of rank one, including zero-rank terms.

source.place: Tag 0FJB (lemma-det-ses), applied in degrees -1 and 0 as in Tag 0FJI.

proof.text: For a finite projective $U$ and arbitrary $V$, specialize the tensor-Hom equivalence with $(M,P,Q)=(U,V,R)$ and remove the right unitor to get $V\otimes U^\vee\cong\operatorname{Hom}_R(U,V)$, with $v\otimes\lambda\mapsto(u\mapsto\lambda(u)v)$. For finite projectives $U,W$, curry a functional on $U\otimes W$ into $\operatorname{Hom}_R(U,W^\vee)$ by the tensor universal property and apply this equivalence with $V=W^\vee$. This gives $(U\otimes W)^\vee\cong U^\vee\otimes W^\vee$, sending $\lambda\otimes\mu$ in the inverse direction to $(u\otimes w\mapsto\lambda(u)\mu(w))$. Finite projective duals and double-dual evaluation are supplied by the dual theorem. Therefore the inverse dual of $\gamma^{-1}$ is an isomorphism from $\det(N^{-1})^\vee\otimes\det(Q^{-1})^\vee$ to $\det(P^{-1})^\vee$. Tensor it with $\gamma^0$, then use the pure-tensor associativity and symmetry maps to obtain the stated $\Gamma_a:D(Q)\otimes D(N)\cong D(P)$. These rearrangements have no signs.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), tensoring gamma^0 and the inverse dual of gamma^(-1); explicit tensor-Hom expansion.

proof.text: Take finite free covers of $N^{-1}$ and $N^0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover]. The chart-descent theorem identifies their top-exterior determinant lines with the annihilator models in [def-trf-projective-determinant-module], compatibly with exterior localization. Write $L=\det_R(N^{-1})$, $M=\det_R(N^0)$. The exterior-algebra maps of $d_N$ and $d_N^{-1}$ are inverse: their composites fix every exterior generator, so equal the identity by the defining uniqueness. They restrict to the annihilator determinant modules: if $x$ annihilates every $n\in N^{-1}$, its image annihilates every $d_Nn\in N^0$, and these exhaust $N^0$. On the free charts these are precisely the top exterior maps; by the chart identifications they give inverse determinant maps $u:L\cong M$ and $u^{-1}$ for the determinant lines used in step 4. Under step 5 the tensor $\delta_N\in M\otimes L^\vee$ is exactly the element corresponding to $u$. The line-duality lemma applies to $L$ by step 4 and makes $R\to\operatorname{End}_R(L)$, $r\mapsto r1_L$, an isomorphism. Composing with $f\mapsto u\circ f$ and the inverse of step 5 gives an isomorphism $t:R\cong D(N)$ taking $1$ to $\delta_N$. Thus $\delta_N$ is a basis element, which is the claimed generator. Line evaluation also identifies duals of all determinant lines as their tensor inverses, justifying the invertible-module terminology for $D(E)$.

source.place: Tag 0FJI (section-determinants-complexes), canonical element of an acyclic complex; Tag 0FJ9 (section-determinants), exterior determinant of an isomorphism.

proof.text: Tensor the isomorphism $t:R\cong D(N)$ with $D(Q)$ and compose with $\Gamma_a$. After the right unitor the resulting map is $F(x)=\Gamma_a(x\otimes\delta_N)$. Its inverse is the composite $D(P)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_a^{-1}}D(Q)\otimes D(N)\xrightarrow{1\otimes t^{-1}}D(Q)\otimes R\cong D(Q)$. Both composites are identities by the inverse equations of $t$ and $\Gamma_a$; call this inverse $T_a$. If $S$ is another inverse, $S=SFT_a=T_a$, giving uniqueness.
